title: ‘America’s Got Talent’ Season 21 Finale Is All Set
summary: The 10 contestants are locked-away for the AGT finale. See who made it through.
body: America voted, the results are in, and the 10 contestants are locked-away for the America’s Got Talent finale. Following the semifinals, six acts collected enough votes to qualify for the final. They are Acro Canine Crew (animal act), Come Here (dancers), Geno Ploeger (magician), Olivia Befus (animal act), Royal Lasers (laser dance act) and Veronika Goroshkova (aerial pole). With those results, the dream ends for contestants Luke Taleno , the Cuba-born rapper; and Travis Garland , a vocalist on Dancing with the Stars . The six selected finalists join four previously-announced Golden Buzzer winners: Hundred Fingers (magic group), Lai Noelle (singer), Nene Royal (singer/musician) and Unitree (robots). Next up, the two-night conclusion of AGT season 21. Each finalist will perform on night one, next Tuesday, Sept. 22, with the results and winner announcement the following night, Wednesday, Sept. 23. What’s at stake is a grand prize of $1 million, along with a headline spot in a Las Vegas live show. This season rung in the changes with a new Judges’ Callbacks round, which gave select performers a second chance to perform before the judges’ chose who to advance for the live …

title: Céline Dion’s Comeback: 5 Takeaways From Night Two Of Her Paris Residency
summary: The Sept. 16 show at Paris' Plenitude Arena proved that there's simply no one quite like Céline Dion.
body: It was just over two years ago that Céline Dion made a public vow: “If I can’t run, I’ll walk. If I can’t walk, I’ll crawl. But I won’t stop.” The declaration was made near the end of Dion’s 2024 documentary I Am: Céline Dion , which chronicled the Canadian superstar’s battle with stiff person syndrome, a rare autoimmune neurological disorder that causes muscle stiffness and painful spasms. This documentary expanded on her 2022 revelation that she had the disease and her 2023 announcement she was cancelling all of her scheduled concerts as she dealt with SPS, a condition that, in a cruel irony, stripped Dion — widely agreed to be one of the greatest singers of all time — of her ability to sing. The scene in which Dion makes this statement happens towards the end of the documentary, near another scene showing her in the midst of a harrowing SPS spasm that leaves her able to communicate only by hand squeezes. The film did not offer, nor assure, a happy ending. And yet, there would be one. Before this week we already knew Dion had come a long way in regaining her health and her voice, via her surprise singing appearance during the…

title: There’s a serious security fix hiding in Google’s September Pixel update
summary: Google has acknowledged that hackers may have already exploited this Pixel security vulnerability.
body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s September Pixel security update patches a cellular modem vulnerability that may have been used in limited, targeted attacks. CVE-2026-58704 could allow a remote attacker to bypass permission checks and escalate privileges without requiring any interaction from the victim. CISA has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list. Google just released the September Pixel Drop , alongside details of its monthly security fixes for Pixel devices. But amid all the new features that stable Android 17 QPR1 brings, one security flaw may have gone unnoticed. Google and other relevant authorities have now confirmed that a Pixel modem vulnerability, which has now been patched, was used in targeted exploitation.

The MCP will soon be available in early access to Google Home Premium Advanced in the US. Last October, the Google Home platform received a significant upgrade with Gemini in copious amounts. While that hasn’t rolled out yet, Google is now announcing a new extension to Google Home’s AI features, making it accessible through AI agents. Today, Google is announcing support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in Google Home. MCP is an open-source standard that allows AI models and chatbots to communicate with — and fetch data from — apps or services easily. The announcement, therefore, means you will soon be able to use a connector to access Google Home’s information through other client apps, including AI chatbots such as Claude, or use resources from Google Home …

title: Older Pixel watches just received a major alarm feature from the Pixel Watch 5
summary: Google is expanding its intelligent Smart Wake alarm feature to previous smartwatch generations to end groggy mornings.
body: Credit: Kaitlyn Cimino / Android Authority TL;DR Google is rolling out the Smart Wake alarm feature to the Pixel Watch 2, 3, and 4 as part of the September 2026 Wear OS 7 update. This feature was originally introduced with the Pixel Watch 5. Smart Wake monitors heart rate and subtle movement for a 30-minute window before your set alarm time, then wakes you with gentle haptic vibrations during lighter sleep phases to reduce morning grogginess. Users can access the feature directly inside the Clock app on their Pixel Watch once it has received the new update. One of the standout quality-of-life features Google introduced with the Pixel Watch 5 launch was Smart Wake, giving users a gentler way to start their mornings. Now, Google is bringing that exact experience to older Pixel Watches. As spotted by Reddit user Broad_Magazine2285 , Smart Wake appears to be rolling out more widely to older Pixel Watches, with confirmations that the feature is going live on the Pixel Watch 4, Pixel Watch 3, and Pixel Watch 2. The feature appears to have rolled out as part of yesterday’s September Wear OS 7 update .

title: Google really wants you to record a video selfie in case you get locked out of your account
summary: Google has begun nudging users to set up video selfies as a backup sign-in method.
body: Credit: Brady Snyder / Android Authority TL;DR Google is actively promoting its new video selfie sign-in method. After rolling the feature out in July, it can be seen prompting users to set up video selfies on the homepage. The feature isn’t meant to replace your passwords or passkeys but to help recover your Google account. After simplifying third-party sign-ups with your Google account and repeatedly urging you to replace passwords with passkeys, Google now wants you to sign in with a selfie video . Google launched the new sign-in method in July, and while it’s still not available in all regions, it can now be seen prompting users to set up login via selfie video. Google has now started soliciting users to try the video selfie sign-in feature via its homepage on desktop. According to Search Engine Watch , the tech giant has started displaying a banner on its homepage to promote the new sign-in method.

title: Meta’s next smart glasses might not attract perverts, or anyone else
summary: Two steps forward, two steps back.
body: TL;DR Meta might be planning to launch a pair of camera-free smart glasses. They could have six microphones for talking to Meta AI and Muse. The smart glasses could be announced at the Meta Connect conference next week. Meta’s smart glasses seem to be everywhere these days, with their cameras and easily modded LEDs making every moment recordable. With glasses like that, in a design that’s nearly indistinguishable from regular sunglasses, the privacy problems practically write themselves. Well, Meta now seems to be considering a new direction for those who don’t want to be seen as creeps out on the street. According to a new report from The Information , Meta is considering launching smart glasses that skip the camera and focus instead on audio and AI features. Internally codenamed “Luna,” the glasses will reportedly feature six microphones, letting users chat with Meta AI and the company’s agentic AI, Muse . They could also include a side button to quickly launch Meta AI and could carry forward the same speaker setup we’ve seen on Meta’s existing smart glasses.

title: 5 Android phones you should buy instead of the iPhone 18 Pro
summary: Maybe leave that Apple in the cart.
body: Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro series a few days ago, and as is often the case with a new iPhone, this year’s changes feel more evolutionary than revolutionary. That’s not necessarily a bad thing. The iPhone 18 Pro still looks incredibly premium, especially in the new Burgundy finish, and the variable-aperture camera is easily one of its more interesting upgrades. But as good as the iPhone 18 Pro looks, it isn’t the only flagship worth spending your money on. Android phones have become incredibly good over the past few years, and depending on what you actually want from your next phone, some alternatives arguably offer even more.

title: I almost missed the Pixel 11’s best camera feature because Google hid it in the settings
summary: Don't spend another minute without the new Quick Access controls.
body: Google’s entire philosophy around the Pixel lineup has been one of simplicity, and that extends to how the Pixel’s camera operates. The idea has always been to create a point-and-shoot experience where you point the phone at something, press the shutter button, and let Google’s software handle the rest. That approach largely works well, but it can also leave you wanting more control when you actually care about how a photo looks. More so, today, when people are looking for a bit more individuality and flavor in photographs. I’m aware of the Pixel camera’s built-in Pro mode, which gives you granular control over shots, but most days I’m not looking to scroll through a long list of manual controls. A few essentials that help me tweak my image without having to get into full manual control territory are what I need.

title: The big Googlebook moment is almost here, and I couldn’t care less
summary: Googlebook has a lot to prove — and Gemini isn't enough.
body: Google’s laptop endeavors are finally getting their long-overdue love. The company is sprucing up the iconic Chromebook ideology into something called Googlebook , which brings together the best of Android and Chrome OS. It carries forward both the good and the bad of its past self, but this time, everything is built around Gemini to give you an AI-first experience. All those big words sound like Google is finally doing something substantial with its laptop efforts. However, the reality is that I couldn’t care less about the Googlebook. Considering the direction Google is putting all its efforts in and how the laptop market is shaping up, I sure wouldn’t bet big on Google’s renewed enthusiasm towards its laptop OS.

title: Android Auto just got a much brighter future in GM vehicles
summary: A clever split-screen setup keeps your phone and truck features together.
body: TL;DR GM’s new infotainment system for the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra keeps Android Auto around despite the company’s earlier plans to move away from it. Android Auto can now run alongside native GM features such as vehicle status and trailering information in a new split-screen layout. The interface will eventually expand across GM’s gas, diesel, and electric vehicles, suggesting Android Auto still has a place in the company’s future. GM’s breakup with Android Auto has been anything but clean. The company first dropped phone projection from newer EVs, then said the same strategy would eventually reach its gas-powered lineup . GM later softened that stance, saying Android Auto and CarPlay would remain available in gas-powered vehicles for the “foreseeable future.” Its latest trucks now suggest that the future could be longer — and more interesting — than expected. The company has unveiled a new infotainment interface for the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra, and Android Auto isn’t merely surviving the redesign. It’s becoming more tightly integrated with GM’s own software.

title: This cheap handheld can emulate games, but also plays your physical GBA cartridges
summary: It won't break the bank, either.
body: Credit: GAMEMT TL;DR The GAMEMT MTX is a new sub-$100 handheld that has a cartridge slot for Game Boy Advance games. It can also emulate SNES, Genesis, PS1, and PSP games via conventional ROM files. The MTX is available at a promotional price of $80 via the official website. The Analogue Pocket still stands out today thanks to its integrated cartridge slot, allowing you to play your physical games on a more modern handheld. Unfortunately, it doesn’t emulate digital game ROMs. But what if you don’t want to choose between a conventional emulation experience and physical cartridges? That’s where the GAMEMT MTX comes in, from the same company that brought you the Pocket Super Knob 5000 . GAMEMT has recently released the MTX (h/t: Retro Handhelds ). This is an emulation-focused handheld that also comes with a Game Boy Advance cartridge slot. This means you can play physical GBA cartridges via emulation, or switch to emulating other consoles via ROM files.

title: Your Android phone is hiding your headphones’ best audio quality — here’s how to unlock it
summary: Android hides a world of Bluetooth codecs. Here's what they do and which matter.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority Your Android phone might be capable of far more Bluetooth audio options than you think. You see, most of the time, Android’s Bluetooth audio menu exposes only a small fraction of what your phone and headphones can actually do. For more advanced settings, you may need to reach for your headphones’ companion app or dive into Android’s Developer Settings , where a much wider selection of Bluetooth codecs and playback modes is available. Take my aging Sony WH-1000XM3, for example. It technically supports Qualcomm’s aptX, yet my phone’s regular Bluetooth settings only offer LDAC as the high-definition option and SBC for standard playback. Some phones don’t even expose an HD codec option at all.

title: 5 features the iPhone Duo shamelessly copied from Android foldables
summary: Eight years of very careful note-taking.
body: It’s been more than eight years since Samsung kicked off the foldable phone era, and a lot has happened since. Motorola, Google, OnePlus, Xiaomi, vivo, OPPO — you name it — almost everyone has had a go at making a foldable. Apple, meanwhile, has spent all these years sitting on the sidelines. But then again, that’s very Apple; it rarely wants to be first. It would rather wait, watch everyone else figure things out, and eventually show up with its own take. And after seeing the iPhone Duo for the first time, it feels like Apple was taking notes the entire time. Credit where it’s due, because there’s a lot here that I already love. The Duo looks ridiculously compact and adorable, a lot like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 . The software optimization Apple showed during the event impressed me, and that barely-there display crease might be one of its biggest wins.
